comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C48-C49. Both evaluations find the chemical induction data (rapamycin and ABA) SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes dose-response data and fold-changes, while peer reviewers accept this as demonstrating versatility of the approach.

Perfect claim overlap (C51-C54) but different emphasis. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED/UNCERTAIN respectively. OpenEval focuses on the systematic optimization and tradeoff documentation, while peer reviewers acknowledge the work but emphasize that parameters remain insufficient for physiological applications and require further optimization.

Perfect agreement on claims C55-C59. Both find the base editing extension SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes differential responses and appropriate tentativeness in speculation, while peer reviewers affirm the adaptability and versatility of the approach across different editing effectors.

Perfect agreement on claims C77-C82. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval characterizes these as appropriate scientific self-critique of limitations, while peer reviewers strongly emphasize these constraints and appreciate that authors clearly describe limitations in the discussion.

High claim overlap (C61-C67, with R6 also including C5-C6). Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes modest effect size and high background requiring optimization, while peer reviewers identify high background and leaky expression as significant weaknesses, emphasizing degraded performance when combining modules.

Strong claim overlap (C44-C47, C50). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes systematic comparison of protein interaction systems and breadth of functional pairs, while peer reviewers affirm this as proof-of-concept for protein-protein interaction control and expansion of the editing toolkit.

Partial overlap (C32-C37). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on the foundational split-pegRNA system with quantitative controls, while peer reviewers group this with the broader strategy comparison (C1-C4, C27-C30) and acknowledge it as the most promising approach achieving high efficiency.

Partial overlap (C41-C43). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes proof-of-concept for protein-mediated control with appropriate negative controls, while peer reviewers accept this as demonstrating protein-protein interaction control of editing.

Partial overlap (C27-C30). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on the negative results being well-controlled and appropriately concluded, while peer reviewers group these with the broader comprehensive approach (C1-C4, C32-C37) and accept the strategy comparison.

Partial overlap (C7, C73-C74). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the core conceptual advance supported by experimental results, while peer reviewers affirm the novelty and conceptual framework as a creative first-of-its-kind approach, though noting practical implementation needs development.

Partial overlap (C75-C76). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes valid comparisons to prior systems and architectural advantages while acknowledging theoretical multiplex capability, while peer reviewers accept the improved modularity and toolkit expansion.

Minimal overlap (C5-C6). Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes modest RNA-dependent effects with high background and appropriate framing as 'potential', while peer reviewers identify this RNA sensing combination as having significant weaknesses requiring optimization due to high background.
